uncited: **Recursive Subdivision:** The 3D domain is recursively divided into sub-volumes.
In standard octrees, each node has 8 children.
**Sparsity Encoding:** Empty regions are represented by null pointers or absence of children, rather than storing zero-valued voxels.
**Hierarchical Traversal:** Rendering or access requires traversing from the root to the leaf.
**Spatial Locality:** Children of a node are spatially contiguous.
**Subtree Merging:** The core differentiator of the DAG family is the identification of structurally identical subtrees (isomorphic nodes) and their replacement with a single shared instance.
This transforms the tree topology into a graph where multiple parents may reference the same child node, eliminating redundancy .
Octrees originated as a spatial partitioning data structure for efficient 3D scene management.
In volume rendering, they were adapted to handle the sparsity of volumetric datasets, where large portions of the domain are empty or uniform.

The Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) became a standard representation for real-time ray tracing and compression, evolving from early pointer-based implementations to more compact implicit and DAG-based variants to reduce memory overhead and improve cache coherence.
